Indore: Dated:- 19/09/2019:-
 Shri Mayank Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioner.
 Shri RS Darbar, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.
Heard with the aid of case diary.
ORDER 1.

This is an application of Petitioner Hitesh Jain under section 438 Cr.P.C seeking anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.272/2017 registered at Police Station -Sadalpur, District-Dhar for the offence punishable under Sections 272, 273, 420, 34 of IPC.
2. Prosecution case in brief is that on 25/07/2019, the Food Inspector visited chiller plant of the petitioner where he was chilling the milk for sell.
He took out 2 samples from Chiller-1 and Chiller-3 containing 1000-600 liters milk respectively and sent them for analysis to the FSL.

On analysis,
both the samples were found sub-standards.
It was also found that the petitioner was selling the milk since last 1 year without obtaining any license.
Therefore, the matter was intimated to the police, who in turn registered the case.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently and repeatedly argued that the petitioner has license for running the business of food product but suppressed the fact that this license was obtained after the samples were taken from his establishment, even he applied for license after the samples were taken from his establishment.

4. It is further argued by the learned counsel that running a business of food article without license is punishable under Section 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and maximum punishment prescribed is 6 months imprisonment and fine up to Rs.5 lacs and selling the sub-standard milk is punishable under Section 51 of the Act, 2006 and maximum penalty prescribed is Rs.5 lacs.
As per Entry-III, part-II of First Schedule of the CRPC, 1973, both the offences are bailable.
Similarly, the offence under Sections 272 & 273 IPC are also bailable, therefore, he be granted anticipatory bail.
